title: The River's Way
logline: One drop of meltwater travels from a glacier to the sea and back to the snow, and never once knows the way.
look: Aerial relief landscape: snow and blue ice, green valleys, golden plains, a silver river; glides and banks, never clipping the land; soft haze for depth.
narrator: female, middle-aged, moderate pitch, american accent
A calm nature documentary narrator, wise and warm
music: Airy strings and soft piano, water and wind beds; a fuller theme over the plains; a hush at the sea; the opening motif returns over the snow.

narration.text: Every river starts as something that couldn't hold on.
It never knows the way. It only knows down.
Mountains, forests, fields. It touches everything and keeps nothing.
When the land splits it, it doesn't argue. It goes both ways.
And at the end, it simply stops being a river.
It becomes the sky. Then, one day, the snow again.
